findingDetails.title: Flow delivery reply conflicts with the global self-scan rule
findingDetails.case: A Flow request reaches its successful delivery step after the board has been written and read back.
findingDetails.evidence: Flow Mode says its reply carries only the board URL and read-back, then prohibits any file output. AGENTS.md exempts Flow from export steps 4–7 but leaves the self-scan step 8 in force; it requires that line beside the path and read-back. The packet skill also says every delivery response carries the self-scan beside an export path and read-back.
findingDetails.userImpact: The Flow response cannot satisfy both instructions: adding the self-scan violates the two-line Flow reply, while omitting it violates the still-active delivery rule.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Direct comparison of AGENTS.md steps 4–8, sk-product-owner/SKILL.md lines 88–104, and Flow Mode Section 6 found the Flow exception stops at steps 4–7 and the reply contract says “and nothing else.”
findingDetails.recommendation: State explicitly whether Flow is exempt from the global HVR self-scan, or revise the Flow reply contract and both runtime instructions so the response shape is consistent.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The root Flow exception explicitly replaces export steps 4–7, and the mode-specific reply says “and nothing else.” That may be intended to override general delivery rules, but it does not name the step 8 HVR rule or resolve the packet skill’s “every delivery response” wording.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Flow may be treated as a non-artifact delivery, making the general artifact scan inapplicable. The current instructions describe the board as a deliverable and do not state that this delivery skips the scan.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: The authoritative instructions explicitly exempt Flow from the global self-scan, or the Flow reply shape is revised to include it without contradicting the board-only contract.
